clue.text: Wanting to keep buzzing off, English leaving part of the 12 20

indicators.note: English leaving means its abbreviation departs from the phrase

parts.note: someone against bees, wanting the buzzing insects kept away, could be called anti-bees

explanation.surface: Someone eager to swat away insects while an Englishman departs a corner of the Mediterranean coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes one E from ANTIBEES. 'the 12 20' points to the linked answer at 12, the coastline between Marseille and Monaco.
explanation.definitionFit: The resort town sits between Nice and Cannes on the Côte d'Azur, so it is one stretch of that coastline.

clue.text: Country, one with capital in Abuja

definitions.text: Country, one with capital in Abuja

parts.note: Niger is a West African country
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the capital, or initial letter, in Abuja

explanation.surface: Naming a nation whose capital city is Abuja.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Abuja is the national capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The West African state has had Abuja as its capital city since 1991.

clue.text: Serious issue with stock stolen by popular author

indicators.note: stolen by means taken into the word for popular

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
BSE, mad cow disease, was a grave problem for livestock

explanation.surface: A popular writer is accused of taking something from a farmer's troubled herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stock' means livestock, not shares; BSE is the cattle disease.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik, the Norwegian dramatist of A Doll's House, is a celebrated playwright and so a writer.

clue.text: European PM embracing male nickname

indicators.note: embracing means the prime minister wraps around the male

parts.note: Pitt, elder or younger, was a British prime minister
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A continental prime minister hugs a man and gives him a pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive byname added to a person's name, like the Great, is a nickname.

clue.text: Living in caravan, I'm a tearaway

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words caravan, I'm a tearaway

explanation.surface: A wild youngster boasts of their lively life on the road in a mobile home.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something alive, as opposed to inert or dead matter; a synonym pair.

clue.text: "Now I shall become mean", having croaked, monsieur?

definitions.meaning: a declaration that one's kindly behaviour is over and toughness begins
a gentleman from Nice who has died is a Nice man who has ceased to exist

explanation.surface: A Frenchman, on his deathbed, vows to turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs on through 7 down. Read cryptically, 'Mr Nice Guy' is a man from Nice, the Riviera city, and once dead he is gone.
explanation.definitionFit: The catchphrase announces an end to being agreeable, which matches deciding to become mean.

clue.text: See 6
Something afoot, follow around one that's suspicious

indicators.note: around says the follow word goes round the rest

parts.note: to tail someone is to follow them

indicators.note: suspicious, as in fishy or not right, signals the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A detective tails a suspect, sensing something is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspicious' scrambles the word one to OEN before 'around' wraps the follow word about it. 'Something afoot' suggests a plot, but read literally it is on a foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail on a toe is literally something on the foot.

clue.text: Safety practice, case of choice blocking device

indicators.note: blocking means the chosen letters sit in the way, inside the device

parts.note: a contraption is a gadget or device

indicators.note: case of takes the outside letters of choice

explanation.surface: A safety procedure where a protective casing jams a machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Safety practice' points to safe sex; 'case of' and 'blocking' look like machine talk but are the selection and insertion signals.
explanation.definitionFit: Birth control is the practice of safe sex, preventing pregnancy.

clue.text: Pay doesn't start for years and years

indicators.note: the word for pay loses its opening letter, so it does not start

parts.note: wages are pay for work

explanation.surface: A salary that never begins arriving seems to take forever.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal phrase for a very long time, matching the colloquial plural sense of long stretches of time.

clue.text: Retailer taking morning or start of evening off

indicators.note: off, as in gone bad or out of order, tells us to rearrange the letters
start of takes only the opening letter of evening

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who skips the morning or the beginning of the evening shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'start of' gives E from evening; 'off' shuffles MORNING + OR + E.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardware dealer selling tools and household metal goods is a kind of shopkeeper.

clue.text: Island insane, might some say? A holiday destination

indicators.note: might some say tells us insane is to be heard as two words, the river name with in before it

parts.note: spoken, insane is heard as in Seine, the Seine being a river of Paris: the in places the island inside

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether an island is mad, then names a sunny getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'insane' heard as 'in Seine' puts I inside FRENCHRIVER (the Seine's description), then A follows. The second word continues at 20 down.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean coast of southern France is a famous playground for holidaymakers.

clue.text: With investment of company, go towards Judas?

indicators.note: investment here means being clothed or enclosed, so the company is wrapped inside

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in taking one's go
at can mean towards, as in throw at

explanation.surface: A businesslike question about whether a company's money is heading to a traitor.
explanation.definitionFit: Judas betrayed Jesus, so his name is a byword for a traitor who switches sides.

clue.text: One's spotted fiddle involving Labour leader in Mr Brown

indicators.note: in places the violin and its contents within the novelist's first name

parts.note: Dan Brown is the author of The Da Vinci Code

indicators.note: involving means the violin takes in the party's first letter

parts.note: an Amati is a violin made by the Cremona family of luthiers

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: A political scandal: a fiddle drawing in the Labour leader, Gordon Brown, gets noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' makes ALMATI, then 'in' sets it inside the novelist's first name. 'Mr Brown' suggests Gordon Brown, the former Labour prime minister, but is Dan Brown of The Da Vinci Code.
explanation.definitionFit: The dog breed is famous for its spotted coat, so one is literally spotted.

clue.text: Cruel, no thanks to the 12?

parts.note: merci is the Gallic word for thanks, the language of 12 across
less means without, so no

explanation.surface: Someone is labelled heartless for not saying thanks in the language of the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the 12' means as said in the language of 12 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no pity, as someone heartless and cruel does; synonyms.

clue.text: Flexible athlete's back after a short breather

indicators.note: after puts the athlete's back letter following the rest
short cuts the last letter off the breathing organ

parts.note: a gill is the organ a fish breathes with

indicators.note: back takes the final letter of athlete's

explanation.surface: A gymnast's spine is supple after a brief pause for breath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breather' is not a rest but a fish's breathing organ; 'short' drops its last letter, and 'after' puts the athlete's last letter at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe moving or bending nimbly and easily; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Goodbye to hello in past narrative

indicators.note: saying goodbye to the greeting means it is removed

parts.note: history is the past
hi is a greeting meaning hello

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell to a greeting in a tale about bygone days.
explanation.definitionFit: A tale or account of events is a narrative; a straight synonym.

clue.text: Territorials waste bully?

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's reserve force
urine is bodily waste

explanation.surface: Reserve soldiers ask whether a thug is a waste of space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bully' is not a thug but 'bull-like', the question mark flagging the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means of or like a bull, which is what bully? playfully suggests.

clue.text: Flat carrier, individual pockets for shopping

indicators.note: pockets means takes inside, so the individual holds the carrier

parts.note: a being is an individual creature
a tray is a flat thing for carrying

explanation.surface: A shopper carries a flat bag, stuffing items into their pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to 'shop' someone is to inform on them to the police; 'shopping' is not about retail here.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses shopping for informing on someone, which is treachery against them.

clue.text: See 12
One going in lower, not both

indicators.note: going in means the one enters the word for lower

parts.note: nether means lower, as in nether regions
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One person goes lower, but the two do not go together.
explanation.definitionFit: The word denies each of two options, so neither one nor the other: the opposite of both.

clue.text: Part of the 12 20 film confined to it, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear says the word is to be spoken and heard

parts.note: a film can is the round tin a reel of film is kept in

explanation.surface: A film locked away on the Riviera.
explanation.walkthrough: The city, home of the film festival, is said like 'can', a film tin.
explanation.definitionFit: The festival city lies on the Côte d'Azur, so it is one piece of that coast.

clue.text: Drink in trailer for cow, perhaps?

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
an ant leaves a scent trail for others to follow, so it is a trailer

explanation.surface: A spirit in a caravan for a cow, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trailer' suggests a caravan or film preview but is an insect that lays trails.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow chews the cud, so it is an example of a cud-chewing mammal; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Struggle to eat animal product for plant eater

indicators.note: to eat means the struggle swallows, so takes inside

parts.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
an egg is produced by an animal

explanation.surface: A herbivore wrestling with whether to eat eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A vegetarian eats plants rather than meat, so is jocularly a plant eater.

clue.text: Show hostility, having to wax lyrical initially

parts.note: to wax is to grow, as the moon does

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of lyrical

explanation.surface: Someone turns aggressive at having to enthuse poetically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wax lyrical' is a single idiom on the surface but splits: 'wax' is grow, and 'lyrical initially' gives L.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog's threatening rumble is a show of hostility; growling at someone signals anger.

clue.text: Characterise type of camera, capturing nothing, say, the wrong way round

indicators.note: capturing means the camera holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a pinhole camera uses a tiny hole instead of a lens

indicators.note: the wrong way round means the zero and the example abbreviation are read backwards

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
e.g. means for example, as say does

explanation.surface: A photographer's instruction about a camera that captures nothing, set up back to front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the wrong way round' makes GEO from the zero and e.g.; 'capturing' sets it within the camera type, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pigeonhole someone is to categorise them, often narrowly, which is to characterise them.

clue.text: Line drawn for missile launcher, old hero in Cuba

parts.note: Che Guevara is revered as a revolutionary hero in Cuba

explanation.surface: A military border drawn for a rocket launcher, with an old Cuban hero involved.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'missile' is a dart and the 'launcher' a darts player; the word is the line players stand behind, darts being a British pub game.
explanation.definitionFit: In darts the throwing line on the floor is marked for the person launching the missiles.

clue.text: Last relative tackled by forward

indicators.note: tackled by means the relative is grabbed and held inside the forward word

parts.note: pert means cheeky or forward
sis is short for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A rugby scene: the last family member brought down by a forward.
explanation.definitionFit: To last is to continue or endure, so both verbs mean carry on.

clue.text: Matelots close to feckless so 12, one gathered

indicators.note: close to takes the final letter of feckless
gathered means the word for so collects the one inside it

parts.note: alors is the word for so in the language of 12 across, Gallic
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Seamen near useless Frenchmen, one of them collected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so 12' means 'so' in the language of 12 across: ALORS takes I inside; 'close to' gives S.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is a slang word for a seaman, borrowed from Gallic; a synonym.
